baselineRegression.method: Seven selected final tests against an isolated turn-start LegalHub copy. All seven fail; 79 other cases excluded. Failures can stop at their first assertion and are not seven independent defects.

changes: Consecutive unsent field patches for the same organization case share one queue item and confirmation promise. Latest values win per field; edits already sent are never mutated. Other-case edits, material writes, creates and deletes form ordering barriers.
Merged failures notify once and restore confirmed state only after the queue drains. Canonical server fields are used directly instead of overwritten with the original unnormalized patch.
New and deleted cases reuse the existing legal operation mutex, error and success handling. Removed duplicate busy state and try/catch/finally flows; synchronous repeated clicks submit once.

Case writes, reminders and plans share JSON request construction and a 15-second abort deadline starting when the request is sent. A rejected timed-out save releases later queued work without retrying the unknown earlier result.
Removed the redundant selected-case ID prop from the workspace, deriving selection from the same active case used for its content.
Strengthened existing rapid-edit, scope-change and create/delete tests, and added merged-failure recovery, interleaved-case ordering and timeout queue-release cases.
preserved: First edits send immediately; create, delete and material operations retain queue order and server confirmation requirements.
Switching the selected case does not cancel its pending saves; closing the hub or switching account/organization invalidates unsent old-scope work.
Personal case storage, reminders, plan payloads, material archive behavior and existing document tools are retained.
All previous prune40 through prune53 changes match their latest recorded fingerprints.
limitations: Mounted production components use mocked network responses; this is not a real server/model/native-client acceptance or a latency benchmark.
Only consecutive unsent patches merge. There is no debounce timer, and a fast server may still receive one request per edit. Personal local storage writes are unchanged.
An abort or missing response cannot undo an already accepted server operation. Timed-out writes are not retried automatically; multiple windows/clients still have no transaction boundary.
No full-suite rerun, backend rebuild, live model calls, visual acceptance, real user data modification, commit, push or client restart.
Personal-case cache ownership, AppContext model read-error/retry presentation and other application partitions remain open.
